correctness.rationale: For each dimension d>=3 the dual faces are precisely vertices, all pairs, two-edge paths and square tetrahedra. Each path triangle belongs to a unique square, so two explicit elementary collapses per square yield the cube 2-skeleton with precisely the long-distance edges added. The cube 2-skeleton is simply connected with free H2 of rank A_d; long edges each add S1, giving B_d. Integral Alexander duality determines the two free reduced homology groups of the ordinary three-cut complex. The full (N-6)-skeleton plus Hurewicz and the Whitehead exact-sequence surjectivity in degree N-4 establish the actual sphere-wedge homotopy type. Verifiers independently confirm all prescribed collapses, mod-two ranks, and small-set face tests for d=3..6. The finite checks do not serve as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: All actual primary and indexed comparisons support novelty for d>=4, not d=3. The indexed three-cube calculation covers only one case, the edge-disjoint-square theorem excludes every higher cube, and planar grid results and total-cut or neighborhood-complex calculations concern different objects. The complete all-dimensional free-face collapse, both wedge multiplicities, and integral two-degree homotopy classification are not implied by any inspected statement; unindexed-equivalence risk remains.

Independent mathematical audit is not performed; conclusions are supported by a complete symbolic proof and finite replay, not external certification.

value.rationale: This determines an entire unbounded and canonical family of ordinary cut complexes, not a single arbitrary small invariant. Unlike the shellable rectangular-grid cases or the edge-disjoint-square theorem, cubes have square overlaps through every edge, and the result explains a stable phenomenon of non-shellability with homology in two consecutive top dimensions. The explicit cubical collapse and rank formulas offer reusable structural control. The d=3 previously known case is not counted as new.
